fact_sheet.business_description: Netflix sells access to entertainment through recurring memberships and an advertising-supported plan across a global distribution system [D02]. It operates as a portfolio business where economics depend on acquiring and retaining an audience across a wide library of licensed and internally commissioned content [D02].
segments_and_mix: Consolidated financials: No separate public subscription and advertising profit segments [D02]
unit_economics: Pricing power: Derived from value delivered compared to alternatives; recent price changes described by management as going well [D00, D04]
Capex intensity: Low physical capex ($688m in 2025), but content cash expenditure is recurrent and significant (approx. 1.1x amortization) [D03, D04]
FCF conversion: FCF of $9.461 billion in 2025; content cash-versus-expense timing is central to earnings-to-FCF comparison [D03]
competitive_position: Share: More than 325 million paid memberships [D02]
Moat evidence: Large audience spreads costs; distribution and recommendation capabilities; content scale [D02]
Peers: YouTube, social video, other streaming services (Disney, Warner Bros. Discovery), games, traditional entertainment [D02, D07]
growth_record_and_outlook: Revenue growth: 15.65% in 2024, 15.85% in 2025, and 16% in Q1 2026 [D03]
Guidance: FY2026 revenue $50.7–51.7 billion (12–14% growth), operating margin 31.5% [D04]
balance_sheet: Net debt: Approx. $5.429 billion at year-end 2025 (Gross debt $14.463 billion less $9.034 billion cash) [D03]
management_and_governance: CEO tenure: Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters are co-CEOs [D02]
Capital allocation record: $9.127 billion repurchased in 2025; abandoned $82.7 billion enterprise value acquisition of Warner operations in 2026 [D03, D08]
Controller/dual-class: Reed Hastings, co-founder, announced he will not seek reelection to the board at the June annual meeting [D02, D04]
price_and_valuation: Drawdown from high: 29.3% from April 1 high [D05]
what_the_market_is_worried_about: Growth moderation and tepid revenue forecasts [D06]
Governance uncertainty following Reed Hastings' planned board departure [D06]
Uncertainty over the next growth driver as the company expands beyond traditional subscription models [D06]
Engagement concerns (aggregate viewing hours growth of 2% in H2 2025) [D06]
Sustainability of premium multiple without Warner synergies [D06]
recent_events: February 26, 2026: Netflix walked away from the Warner transaction after a superior offer was made [D08]
April 16, 2026: Reported Q1 results and announced Reed Hastings will not stand for reelection [D04]
April 17, 2026: Share price fell over 10% following earnings/forecast release [D06, D08]
pershing_context: Fund AUM: $19.748 billion core-fund AUM as of Feb 2026 [D09]
Current holdings: Amazon, Meta, Hertz, Alphabet, Brookfield, Uber, Restaurant Brands, Universal Music, Howard Hughes, Fannie/Freddie [D09]
Existing stake: Sold entire Netflix position in April 2022 [D00]
Any prior engagement: Not in pack

barriers_to_entry.evidence: As the leading global streamer with over 325 million members, its scale in content production and recommendation technology creates significant barriers [D02].

limited_extrinsic_exposure.evidence: Revenue is driven by global memberships and advertising, showing resilience despite competitive pressures [D02, D03].

strong_financial_profile.evidence: With net debt of approximately $5.429 billion against a market cap of over $400 billion, the leverage profile is conservative [D03, D05].

minimal_capital_markets_dependency.evidence: The company is self-funding, evidenced by $9.127 billion in share repurchases in 2025 [D03].

large_market_cap.evidence: The market capitalization is approximately $407.58 billion, well above the $10 billion threshold [D05].

attractive_valuation_screen.evidence: While the stock has experienced a 29.3% drawdown, the forward valuation relative to peers and the S&P 500 is not explicitly defined in the pack [D05, D06].

management_governance.evidence: The upcoming departure of co-founder Reed Hastings from the board introduces governance uncertainty that needs further assessment [D04, D06].

durable_growth_runway.evidence: The company continues to demonstrate double-digit revenue growth and is expanding into advertising-supported models [D03, D04].

gate1.one_line_business_quality_verdict: a dominant, free-cash-flow-generative global streaming leader with massive scale and a proven ability to self-fund growth.

gate2.variant_perception: The market views the recent growth moderation, Reed Hastings' departure, and the failed Warner acquisition as structural threats to Netflix's premium valuation [D06]. The 29.3% drawdown provides a compelling entry point for a business that remains the dominant global streaming player with significant pricing power and self-funding capability [D02, D05].

gate4.catalyst_description: We expect a re-rating as the market recognizes the durability of Netflix's double-digit revenue growth and consistent free-cash-flow generation [D03, D04], moving past the irrational pessimism surrounding management transition and the failed Warner acquisition [D06].
levers_or_steps: Maintain disciplined content investment to drive subscriber retention and engagement [D02]
Scale advertising-supported models to unlock additional revenue streams [D02, D04]
Continue rigorous capital allocation, utilizing strong FCF to repurchase shares at attractive valuation levels [D03]
gate4.why_this_role_fits_the_era: In our 'Pershing Square 3.0' era, we focus on quality compounders with dominant market positions. Netflix is a self-funding global leader that has successfully navigated a temporary dislocation; our role is to lean into the long-term compounding of FCF rather than initiating public activism [D02, D03, D05].

kill_criteria: Operating margins compress below 30% due to inefficient content spend or increased competitive churn [D02, D04]
Subscriber growth turns negative on an annual basis as the advertising model fails to offset saturation in core markets [D02, D04]
Management abandons the disciplined, self-funding capital allocation policy in favor of debt-fueled M&A or excessive share dilution [D03, D04]

gate5.portfolio_fit: This fits our 'Pershing Square 3.0' focus on dominant, FCF-generative quality compounders [D02, D03]. While we currently hold other technology-adjacent names like Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta, Netflix provides distinct exposure to the pure-play entertainment streaming segment [D09].
gate5.liquidity_assessment: Given the market capitalization of approximately $407.58 billion and consistent trading activity, we can build a core position over several weeks without significant market impact [D05].
gate5.biggest_risk_in_one_sentence: The market's perception of a permanent growth slowdown, combined with governance uncertainty post-Hastings, could lead to sustained multiple compression if the company fails to reignite subscriber engagement and advertising revenue growth [D04, D06].

valuation.eps_path: 12-14% revenue growth guidance and margin resilience driving double-digit FCF growth
valuation.downside_case: Multiple contraction to 15-18x if margins erode below 30% or dominant position is impaired

drivers.driver: Netflix is a dominant, free-cash-flow-generative global streaming leader with a massive, hard-to-replicate content and technology moat [D02, D03].
The business exhibits simple, predictable, subscription-based economics with strong 32.3% operating margins and a robust self-funding capability [D02, D03].
The recent 29.3% drawdown presents a compelling entry point for a premium business that has successfully transitioned to an advertising-supported growth model [D02, D05].
Management’s disciplined capital allocation is evidenced by the $9.127 billion returned through share repurchases in 2025 and the prudent decision to walk away from an overvalued M&A deal [D03, D08].

kill_criteria: Operating margins compress below 30% due to inefficient content spend or increased competitive churn [D02, D04]
Subscriber growth turns negative on an annual basis as the advertising model fails to offset saturation [D02, D04]
Management abandons the disciplined, self-funding capital allocation policy in favor of debt-fueled M&A or excessive share dilution [D03, D04]

final.what_would_change_our_mind: A fundamental erosion of Netflix’s dominant global streaming position, a breakdown in disciplined capital allocation following the leadership transition, or a sustained inability to grow viewing hours and advertising revenue.
final.memo:
Netflix remains the dominant global streaming leader, commanding over 325 million paid memberships through its unparalleled content library and superior recommendation technology [D02]. The business is highly free-cash-flow-generative, producing $9.461 billion in FCF during 2025, which allows the company to self-fund its growth while consistently returning capital to shareholders [D03]. Its ability to maintain margins at or above 31.5% while expanding its advertising-supported model confirms our view of it as a high-quality, predictable compounder [D02, D04].

Recent market volatility, including a 29.3% drawdown from its April high, has created a significant dislocation in Netflix's valuation [D05]. The market is fixated on short-term governance concerns following the co-founder's departure and the failed attempt at a major acquisition, incorrectly viewing these as structural impairments [D04, D06, D08]. We believe the market is failing to appreciate the strength of the underlying franchise, which continues to demonstrate double-digit revenue growth and dominant market scale [D02, D03].

At a trailing P/E of 37.5x, the stock is attractively priced relative to its long-term compounding potential [D05]. With a growth algorithm driven by disciplined content spend, pricing power, and ongoing share repurchases, we model a compelling IRR of approximately 22% [D03, D04, D05]. We believe the market will eventually re-rate the business as the durability of its FCF generation becomes more evident over the next three years [D03, D04].

Our role is to lean into this high-quality compounder as the market looks past recent irrational pessimism [D06]. We will continue to monitor the company’s operating margins and engagement metrics as key indicators of continued dominance [D02, D04, D06]. Risks include a potential margin compression due to content inefficiencies or a failure of the advertising model to offset market saturation, both of which would force us to re-evaluate our position [D02, D04].

We are initiating a target position of 8% of NAV, reflecting our high conviction in Netflix’s long-term intrinsic value [D05]. This position will be built systematically to capture the current market dislocation [D05].
